html:
The Chinchorro were fishing peoples of the Atacama coast of northern Chile and southern Peru who, from about 5000 BCE, made the oldest known artificial mummies in the world.

They took apart the bodies of the dead, men, women and children alike, packed them with plants, clay and sticks, and covered them with clay masks painted black or red. They did this some two thousand years before the Egyptians began to mummify. The dry desert preserved hundreds of these bodies around today's Arica.

Why they did it is unknown; it may have kept the dead present among the living. Their sites became a World Heritage Site in 2021. They show that complex beliefs about death arose among hunters and fishers of Chile long before farming states, and long before the Inca or the people of the Atacama oases.
sum: The Chinchorro were fishing peoples of the Atacama coast of northern Chile and southern Peru who, from about 5000 BCE, made the oldest known artificial mummies in the world.
